h1.en: How Much Does IVF Cost in Oregon in 2026?
h1.es: ¿Cuánto Cuesta la FIV en Oregón en 2026?

subhero.en: A single IVF cycle in Oregon costs $12,000 to $30,000 out of pocket in 2026, depending on the clinic, protocol, medications, and add-ons. Oregon does not have a state insurance mandate requiring coverage of IVF, meaning most Oregon residents without employer-sponsored fertility benefits pay the full amount themselves. Medications, preimplantation genetic testing, and frozen embryo transfers are typically billed separately on top of the base cycle fee. Oregon's HB4155 (2026) would have required commercial insurers and the state public employee benefit boards to cover IVF, but the bill died in the Joint Ways and Means Committee before the 2026 session adjourned.
subhero.es: Un solo ciclo de FIV en Oregón cuesta de $12,000 a $30,000 de bolsillo en 2026, dependiendo de la clínica, el protocolo, los medicamentos y los complementos. Oregón no tiene un mandato estatal de seguro que requiera cobertura de FIV, lo que significa que la mayoría de los residentes de Oregón sin beneficios de fertilidad patrocinados por el empleador pagan el monto total por su cuenta. Los medicamentos, las pruebas genéticas preimplantacionales y las transferencias de embriones congelados generalmente se facturan por separado además de la tarifa base del ciclo.

quickAnswer.en: In 2026, a standard IVF cycle in Oregon costs $12,000 to $15,000 for the base procedure at independent Portland-area fertility clinics, plus $3,000 to $7,000 in fertility medications, for an all-in total of $15,000 to $22,000 per cycle. Hospital-affiliated and national-network centers such as OHSU-affiliated Spring Fertility and Oregon Fertility Institute can run $15,000 to $30,000 all-in. Oregon has no state insurance mandate for IVF as of mid-2026, so coverage depends entirely on individual employer benefits, voluntary plan inclusions, or fertility-benefit platforms like Progyny or Carrot. Medicare does not cover IVF under any Part. The Oregon Health Plan (OHP), Oregon's Medicaid program, excludes IVF from its Prioritized List of covered services. Self-pay patients have the right to a written Good Faith Estimate before treatment begins under the No Surprises Act.
quickAnswer.es: En 2026, un ciclo estándar de FIV en Oregón cuesta de $12,000 a $15,000 por el procedimiento base en clínicas de fertilidad independientes en el área de Portland, más $3,000 a $7,000 en medicamentos de fertilidad, para un total de $15,000 a $22,000 por ciclo. Los centros afiliados a hospitales y de redes nacionales pueden costar de $15,000 a $30,000 en total. Oregón no tiene un mandato estatal de seguro para FIV a mediados de 2026. Medicare no cubre la FIV bajo ninguna Parte. El Oregon Health Plan (OHP), el programa Medicaid de Oregón, excluye la FIV de su Lista Priorizada de servicios cubiertos. Los pacientes que pagan de su bolsillo tienen derecho a un Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito antes de comenzar el tratamiento.

introParagraphs.en: Oregon remains one of the states without a comprehensive insurance mandate for in vitro fertilization in 2026. While 25 states and the District of Columbia now require some level of private insurance coverage for fertility treatments, Oregon is not among them. The 2026 Oregon legislature considered HB4155, which would have required commercial insurers, the Oregon Educators Benefit Board, and the Public Employees' Benefit Board to cover fertility services including IVF with a minimum of three egg retrievals. The bill received committee approval and bipartisan support but died in the Joint Ways and Means Committee before the session adjourned, according to the RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association tracking page for Oregon. Oregon patients should review their employer plan documents carefully, as some large employers voluntarily include fertility benefits or contract with fertility-benefit platforms like Progyny, Carrot, or Maven, regardless of any state mandate.
introParagraphs.es: Oregón sigue siendo uno de los estados sin un mandato de seguro integral para la fertilización in vitro en 2026. Si bien 25 estados y el Distrito de Columbia ahora requieren algún nivel de cobertura de seguro privado para tratamientos de fertilidad, Oregón no está entre ellos. Los pacientes de Oregón deben revisar sus documentos del plan de empleador cuidadosamente, ya que algunos grandes empleadores incluyen voluntariamente beneficios de fertilidad o contratan con plataformas de beneficios de fertilidad como Progyny, Carrot o Maven, independientemente de cualquier mandato estatal.

introParagraphs.en: The Oregon Health Plan (OHP), Oregon's Medicaid program administered by the Oregon Health Authority, does not cover IVF. Effective February 1, 2026, OHP covers services through Prioritized List lines 1 through 470, and infertility treatment is excluded from that list. Oregon's Reproductive Health Equity Act (RHEA), passed in 2017, requires insurers to cover abortion, contraception, and postpartum care at no out-of-pocket cost, but the RHEA does not address infertility or assisted reproductive technology. Self-pay or uninsured Oregon patients considering IVF should first check whether they qualify for any cost-assistance programs and review their rights under the No Surprises Act before scheduling treatment. The federal patient-provider dispute resolution process at cms.gov/nosurprisesact applies to all Oregon fertility providers regardless of plan type.
introParagraphs.es: El Oregon Health Plan (OHP), el programa Medicaid de Oregón administrado por la Oregon Health Authority, no cubre la FIV. A partir del 1 de febrero de 2026, OHP cubre los servicios a través de las líneas 1 a 470 de la Lista Priorizada, y el tratamiento de infertilidad está excluido de esa lista. La Ley de Equidad en Salud Reproductiva de Oregón (RHEA), aprobada en 2017, requiere que las aseguradoras cubran el aborto, los anticonceptivos y la atención posparto sin costos de bolsillo, pero la RHEA no aborda la infertilidad ni la tecnología de reproducción asistida.

introParagraphs.en: Portland and the broader Oregon market feature several well-established fertility clinics. The Portland-area landscape in 2026 includes Pinnacle Fertility (formerly ORM Fertility), Spring Fertility Portland (which partners with OHSU for patient transitions), Oregon Fertility Institute, and the Fertility Center of Oregon. Published self-pay rates for a base IVF cycle at these clinics range from approximately $12,000 to $15,000 at independent centers to $15,000 and above at hospital-affiliated or national-network locations. This guide covers what IVF costs in Oregon in 2026, the current state insurance landscape, how to request a Good Faith Estimate from an Oregon fertility clinic, and the self-pay options available to patients without employer-sponsored coverage. Uninsured patients should also review whether they qualify for any federal assistance programs and consult the No Surprises Act resources at healthcare.gov.
introParagraphs.es: Portland y el mercado más amplio de Oregón cuentan con varias clínicas de fertilidad bien establecidas. El panorama del área de Portland en 2026 incluye Pinnacle Fertility (anteriormente ORM Fertility), Spring Fertility Portland (que se asocia con OHSU), Oregon Fertility Institute y el Fertility Center of Oregon. Las tarifas de pago propio publicadas para un ciclo de FIV base en estas clínicas oscilan entre aproximadamente $12,000 y $15,000 en centros independientes hasta $15,000 o más en ubicaciones afiliadas a hospitales o de redes nacionales. Esta guía cubre lo que cuesta la FIV en Oregón en 2026, el panorama actual del seguro estatal, cómo solicitar un Estimado de Buena Fe de una clínica de fertilidad de Oregón y las opciones de pago propio disponibles para pacientes sin cobertura patrocinada por el empleador.

explanationParagraphs.en: Oregon independent fertility clinics and hospital-affiliated centers differ significantly in cost structure. The 2026 Oregon pricing chart above shows that independent clinics such as the Fertility Center of Oregon (which publishes a global fee of approximately $12,500 that includes monitoring, retrieval, and one transfer with cryopreservation) are typically 25 to 50 percent less expensive than hospital-affiliated centers. Spring Fertility Portland, which collaborates with OHSU for patient transitions, and Oregon Fertility Institute fall in the mid-range to higher end of Oregon pricing, with total all-in costs (including medications) running $18,000 to $30,000 per cycle depending on protocol complexity. The clinical procedure itself, egg retrieval, fertilization, embryo culture, and embryo transfer, is equivalent across settings. The price differential reflects overhead structure, lab infrastructure, and ancillary billing practices, not measurable quality differences for most patient populations.
explanationParagraphs.es: Las clínicas de fertilidad independientes de Oregón y los centros afiliados a hospitales difieren significativamente en su estructura de costos. La tabla de precios de Oregón 2026 anterior muestra que las clínicas independientes, como el Fertility Center of Oregon (que publica una tarifa global de aproximadamente $12,500), son típicamente un 25 a 50 por ciento menos costosas que los centros afiliados a hospitales. El procedimiento clínico en sí es equivalente en todos los entornos. La diferencia de precio refleja la estructura de gastos generales, la infraestructura de laboratorio y las prácticas de facturación ancilares.

explanationParagraphs.en: Oregon base cycle prices cover the retrieval, fertilization, embryo culture, and one fresh transfer at most clinics. Fertility medications are almost always billed separately and add $3,000 to $7,000 per cycle depending on the stimulation protocol. Optional components, including preimplantation genetic testing (PGT), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), embryo cryopreservation, and annual embryo storage, are itemized separately at every Oregon clinic reviewed for this guide. Frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles are substantially cheaper because the egg retrieval and fertilization steps were completed in a prior cycle, and most Oregon clinics charge $3,500 to $6,000 for a FET. Because Oregon has no state mandate, self-pay patients should request a complete itemized written quote, a Good Faith Estimate, before signing any financial agreement.
explanationParagraphs.es: Los precios del ciclo base de Oregón cubren la recuperación, la fertilización, el cultivo de embriones y una transferencia fresca en la mayoría de las clínicas. Los medicamentos de fertilidad casi siempre se facturan por separado y agregan $3,000 a $7,000 por ciclo. Los componentes opcionales, incluyendo las pruebas genéticas preimplantacionales (PGT), la inyección intracitoplasmática de espermatozoides (ICSI), la criopreservación de embriones y el almacenamiento anual de embriones, se detallan por separado en cada clínica de Oregón. Los ciclos de transferencia de embriones congelados (TEC) son sustancialmente más baratos porque los pasos de recuperación y fertilización se completaron en un ciclo anterior.

explanationParagraphs.en: The practical takeaway for Oregon self-pay IVF patients in 2026: independent clinics in the Portland metro area offer base cycle rates 25 to 50 percent below hospital-affiliated center rates for a clinically comparable procedure. Patients who do not have employer-sponsored coverage should compare at least two to three Oregon clinic quotes, ask explicitly for the self-pay cash price and whether a prompt-payment discount applies, and confirm whether anesthesia, laboratory fees, and monitoring visits are bundled or itemized separately. Clinic pricing varies significantly, and a Good Faith Estimate in writing is the only reliable protection against unexpected bill inflation after treatment.
explanationParagraphs.es: La conclusión práctica para los pacientes de FIV de pago propio en Oregón en 2026: las clínicas independientes en el área metropolitana de Portland ofrecen tarifas de ciclo base un 25 a 50 por ciento por debajo de las tarifas de los centros afiliados a hospitales para un procedimiento clínicamente comparable. Los pacientes que no tienen cobertura patrocinada por el empleador deben comparar al menos dos o tres cotizaciones de clínicas de Oregón, preguntar explícitamente por el precio de pago en efectivo de pago propio y si aplica un descuento por pago puntual.

paragraphs.en: Medicare does not cover IVF under any part of the program, including Original Medicare Part A (hospital inpatient), Medicare Part B (outpatient and physician services), or Part D (prescription drugs). This federal program-level exclusion applies equally in Oregon. The 2026 Medicare Part B deductible of $283 and the standard 20% coinsurance apply only to services Medicare actually covers; because IVF is entirely excluded, no Medicare deductible or coinsurance calculation applies to an IVF bill. Medicare Advantage plans are not required to add IVF as a supplemental benefit, though a small number of Medicare Advantage plans voluntarily offer limited fertility-related extras. Oregon patients on Medicare should check their specific plan's Summary of Benefits for any supplemental fertility benefit language. Medigap supplemental plans also do not cover IVF because Medigap covers only the cost-sharing that applies to services Original Medicare pays for.
paragraphs.es: Medicare no cubre la FIV bajo ninguna parte del programa, incluyendo el Medicare Original Parte A (hospitalización), Medicare Parte B (ambulatorio y servicios médicos) ni la Parte D (medicamentos recetados). Esta exclusión a nivel de programa federal aplica igualmente en Oregón. El deducible de Medicare Parte B 2026 de $283 y el coseguro estándar del 20% solo aplican a los servicios que Medicare realmente cubre; como la FIV está completamente excluida, no aplica ningún cálculo de deducible o coseguro de Medicare. Los planes Medicare Advantage no están obligados a agregar la FIV como beneficio suplementario. Los planes Medigap tampoco cubren la FIV porque el Medigap cubre solo los costos compartidos que aplican a los servicios que paga el Medicare Original.

paragraphs.en: The Oregon Health Plan (OHP), Oregon's Medicaid program administered by the Oregon Health Authority, does not cover IVF as of mid-2026. OHP's Prioritized List of Health Services, which determines covered benefits, excludes infertility treatment. The 2026 Oregon legislative session considered HB4155, which would have required state employee benefit boards and commercial insurers to cover IVF, but the bill died in the Joint Ways and Means Committee before the session adjourned, according to RESOLVE's Oregon bill tracking. ACA-compliant plans sold through Oregon's health insurance marketplace do not have a federal requirement to cover IVF; the Affordable Care Act lists essential health benefits but fertility treatment is not among them at the federal level. Oregon employers may voluntarily include IVF coverage, and some large Oregon employers contract with fertility-benefit platforms such as Progyny, Carrot, or Maven that provide IVF coverage regardless of the absence of a state mandate. Oregon patients who purchase individual coverage through the ACA marketplace should review their specific plan's Summary of Benefits and Coverage to check for any voluntary fertility benefit.
paragraphs.es: El Oregon Health Plan (OHP), el programa Medicaid de Oregón administrado por la Oregon Health Authority, no cubre la FIV a mediados de 2026. La Lista Priorizada de Servicios de Salud de OHP, que determina los beneficios cubiertos, excluye el tratamiento de infertilidad. La sesión legislativa de Oregón 2026 consideró HB4155, que habría requerido que los consejos de beneficios de empleados estatales y las aseguradoras comerciales cubrieran la FIV, pero el proyecto de ley murió en el Comité Conjunto de Vías y Medios antes de que la sesión se levantara. Los planes ACA-compliant vendidos a través del mercado de seguros de salud de Oregón no tienen un requisito federal de cubrir la FIV.

paragraphs.en: Under the No Surprises Act, effective January 1, 2022, any Oregon patient paying cash or who is uninsured has the right to a written Good Faith Estimate from the fertility clinic or hospital before the IVF procedure begins. For an Oregon IVF treatment cycle scheduled at least 10 business days out, the provider must furnish the Good Faith Estimate at least 3 business days before service. For appointments scheduled 3 to 9 business days out, the Good Faith Estimate arrives at least 1 business day before service. Oregon fertility clinics, including independent clinics and hospital-affiliated centers, are required to comply. The federal consumer guidance and the patient-provider dispute resolution portal are available at cms.gov/nosurprisesact. A Good Faith Estimate for Oregon IVF must itemize the base cycle, medications if dispensed by the clinic, anesthesia, laboratory fees, and any optional add-ons agreed to by the patient, such as PGT or ICSI.
paragraphs.es: Bajo la Ley de No Sorpresas, vigente desde el 1 de enero de 2022, cualquier paciente de Oregón que pague en efectivo o no tenga seguro tiene derecho a un Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito de la clínica de fertilidad u hospital antes de que comience el procedimiento de FIV. Para un ciclo de tratamiento de FIV en Oregón programado al menos 10 días hábiles antes, el proveedor debe proporcionar el Estimado de Buena Fe al menos 3 días hábiles antes del servicio. Para citas programadas de 3 a 9 días hábiles antes, el Estimado de Buena Fe llega al menos 1 día hábil antes del servicio. La guía federal para el consumidor y el portal de resolución de disputas entre paciente y proveedor están disponibles en cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

paragraphs.en: To request a Good Faith Estimate for IVF at an Oregon fertility clinic in 2026, follow these steps: (1) Contact the clinic's financial coordinator and identify yourself as self-pay or uninsured, or confirm you want an itemized pre-treatment cost estimate even if you have insurance. (2) Request a written Good Faith Estimate listing the base cycle code (HCPCS S4015 for a fresh cycle, S4016 for a frozen cycle), anesthesia, laboratory fees, monitoring visit fees, and all optional add-ons such as ICSI, PGT, and embryo storage. (3) Provide your ZIP code and share the specific protocol your Oregon reproductive endocrinologist has recommended. (4) Confirm the timing: if your retrieval is scheduled 10 or more business days out, you are entitled to the estimate at least 3 business days in advance; if scheduled 3 to 9 business days out, at least 1 business day in advance. (5) Keep the written Good Faith Estimate. If your final Oregon IVF bill exceeds the estimate by $400 or more, you have the right to submit a patient-provider dispute resolution (PPDR) claim within 120 days of the bill date through the federal portal at cms.gov/nosurprisesact.
paragraphs.es: Para solicitar un Estimado de Buena Fe para FIV en una clínica de fertilidad de Oregón en 2026, siga estos pasos: (1) Comuníquese con el coordinador financiero de la clínica e identifíquese como paciente de pago propio o sin seguro. (2) Solicite un Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito que liste el código del ciclo base (HCPCS S4015 para ciclo fresco, S4016 para ciclo congelado), anestesia, honorarios de laboratorio, honorarios de visitas de monitoreo y todos los complementos opcionales como ICSI, PGT y almacenamiento de embriones. (3) Proporcione su código postal y comparta el protocolo específico que su endocrinólogo reproductivo de Oregón ha recomendado. (4) Confirme el calendario: si su recuperación está programada 10 o más días hábiles antes, tiene derecho al estimado al menos 3 días hábiles de antelación; si está programada de 3 a 9 días hábiles antes, al menos 1 día hábil de antelación. (5) Conserve el Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito. Si su factura final de FIV en Oregón supera el estimado en $400 o más, tiene derecho a presentar una reclamación PPDR dentro de 120 días desde la fecha de la factura a través del portal federal en cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

paragraphs.en: A Good Faith Estimate for Oregon IVF is not a guaranteed final bill. Common reasons the actual charges exceed the estimate include: additional monitoring appointments required by your specific stimulation response, medication adjustments mid-cycle based on follicle development, unexpected embryo development outcomes requiring a different number of PGT biopsies, anesthesia billed separately by a provider not included in the clinic's base package, and storage fees for additional embryos beyond what the original estimate assumed. If the final Oregon IVF bill exceeds the Good Faith Estimate by $400 or more, the patient has 120 days from the bill date to file a PPDR claim at cms.gov/nosurprisesact. Commercial insurance patients in Oregon who receive an unexpected bill after the chargemaster rate is applied should also check whether the No Surprises Act balance-billing protections apply to their provider's network status.
paragraphs.es: Un Estimado de Buena Fe para la FIV en Oregón no es una factura final garantizada. Las razones comunes por las que los cargos reales superan el estimado incluyen: citas de monitoreo adicionales requeridas por su respuesta de estimulación específica, ajustes de medicamentos a mitad del ciclo basados en el desarrollo folicular, resultados inesperados del desarrollo embrionario que requieren un número diferente de biopsias de PGT, anestesia facturada por separado por un proveedor no incluido en el paquete base de la clínica, y tarifas de almacenamiento para embriones adicionales más allá de lo que asumió el estimado original. Si la factura final de FIV en Oregón supera el Estimado de Buena Fe en $400 o más, el paciente tiene 120 días desde la fecha de la factura para presentar una reclamación PPDR en cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

paragraphs.en: Oregon patients who have employer-sponsored insurance should verify their coverage before assuming they must pay out of pocket for IVF. Oregon employers, especially large technology companies, hospital systems, and state government employers, frequently include fertility benefits voluntarily through platforms such as Progyny or Carrot. Spring Fertility Portland, for example, accepts insurance from Progyny, Carrot, Cigna, Aetna, Providence Health Plan, First Choice Health, Kaiser Permanente, Moda Health, Maven, United Healthcare, and Blue Cross Blue Shield, among others. Patients with commercial insurance should request a pre-authorization determination in writing before beginning an IVF cycle, as high-dose stimulation medications and the IVF procedure itself typically require prior authorization on most commercial plans. An ACA-compliant plan purchased through the Oregon marketplace may include IVF as a voluntary benefit; check the plan's Summary of Benefits and Coverage document for the fertility benefit section.
paragraphs.es: Los pacientes de Oregón que tienen seguro patrocinado por el empleador deben verificar su cobertura antes de asumir que deben pagar de su bolsillo por la FIV. Los empleadores de Oregón, especialmente las grandes empresas de tecnología, los sistemas hospitalarios y los empleadores del gobierno estatal, frecuentemente incluyen beneficios de fertilidad voluntariamente a través de plataformas como Progyny o Carrot. Los pacientes con seguro comercial deben solicitar una determinación de preautorización por escrito antes de comenzar un ciclo de FIV, ya que los medicamentos de estimulación y el procedimiento de FIV en sí generalmente requieren autorización previa en la mayoría de los planes comerciales.

items.en: Oregon employer plan type and fertility benefit coverage: Oregon has no state mandate for IVF as of mid-2026, so coverage depends entirely on whether your employer voluntarily includes IVF, contracts with a fertility-benefit platform like Progyny or Carrot, or offers a health plan that includes it as an optional benefit. Review your Summary of Benefits and Coverage or contact HR before assuming you must pay self-pay rates.
items.es: Tipo de plan de empleador de Oregón y cobertura de beneficios de fertilidad: Oregón no tiene mandato estatal para FIV a mediados de 2026, por lo que la cobertura depende enteramente de si su empleador incluye voluntariamente la FIV, contrata con una plataforma de beneficios de fertilidad como Progyny o Carrot, u ofrece un plan de salud que la incluye como beneficio opcional.

items.en: Clinic type in Oregon: independent fertility clinics in Portland (such as the Fertility Center of Oregon with a published global fee around $12,500) typically charge $12,000 to $15,000 for a base cycle; hospital-affiliated or national-network centers (such as Spring Fertility Portland and Oregon Fertility Institute) typically charge $15,000 to $22,000 for comparable base cycles before medications and add-ons.
items.es: Tipo de clínica en Oregón: las clínicas de fertilidad independientes en Portland (como el Fertility Center of Oregon con una tarifa global publicada de aproximadamente $12,500) típicamente cobran $12,000 a $15,000 por un ciclo base; los centros afiliados a hospitales o de redes nacionales típicamente cobran $15,000 a $22,000 por ciclos base comparables antes de medicamentos y complementos.

items.en: Medication protocol and stimulation response: higher ovarian stimulation doses mean higher medication costs ($3,000 to $7,000 per cycle). Poor responders may require multiple retrieval attempts, each resetting the medication cost. Specialty pharmacy discounts and clinic-dispensed medication programs can reduce medication costs by 10 to 30 percent versus retail pharmacy pricing.
items.es: Protocolo de medicación y respuesta de estimulación: las dosis más altas de estimulación ovárica significan costos de medicamentos más altos ($3,000 a $7,000 por ciclo). Las personas con baja respuesta pueden requerir múltiples intentos de recuperación, cada uno reiniciando el costo de medicamentos.

items.en: Number of cycles needed: average success rates per cycle vary by age and diagnosis. Oregon patients under 35 have higher per-cycle success rates than those over 40. Many patients require 2 to 3 cycles to achieve a live birth, which can multiply total out-of-pocket costs to $30,000 to $90,000 or more over the course of treatment.
items.es: Número de ciclos necesarios: las tasas de éxito promedio por ciclo varían según la edad y el diagnóstico. Muchos pacientes requieren 2 a 3 ciclos para lograr un nacimiento vivo, lo que puede multiplicar los costos totales de bolsillo a $30,000 a $90,000 o más.

items.en: Independent Oregon fertility clinic cash bundles and multi-cycle packages: several Portland-area clinics offer multi-cycle packages or shared-risk programs at bundled rates that are 15 to 25 percent less expensive per cycle than single-cycle pricing. Ask the financial coordinator explicitly about multi-cycle pricing and whether a 100-percent refund program is available.
items.es: Paquetes en efectivo de clínicas de fertilidad independientes de Oregón y paquetes de múltiples ciclos: varias clínicas del área de Portland ofrecen paquetes de múltiples ciclos o programas de riesgo compartido a tarifas agrupadas que son un 15 a 25 por ciento menos costosas por ciclo que los precios de ciclo único.

items.en: Chargemaster discount ask for self-pay patients: Oregon fertility clinics, like all healthcare providers, maintain a published chargemaster rate (the full list price). Self-pay patients who identify themselves before treatment and offer prompt payment can often negotiate 10 to 25 percent off the listed base cycle fee. Ask the financial coordinator directly: 'What is your self-pay cash price, and is there a same-day payment discount?' Get the answer in writing as part of the Good Faith Estimate.
items.es: Solicitud de descuento en el arancel para pacientes de pago propio: las clínicas de fertilidad de Oregón, como todos los proveedores de atención médica, mantienen una tarifa de arancel publicada (el precio de lista completo). Los pacientes de pago propio que se identifican antes del tratamiento y ofrecen pago puntual a menudo pueden negociar un 10 a 25 por ciento de descuento en la tarifa del ciclo base listada.

items.en: Sliding-scale FQHC and fertility grant programs: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) in Oregon do not typically perform IVF, but fertility grants through RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association and Baby Quest Foundation can reduce out-of-pocket costs by $1,500 to $15,000 for qualifying patients. Sliding-scale fees at FQHCs may apply to infertility diagnostic testing (bloodwork, ultrasound, hormone panels) even if IVF itself is not available at those sites.
items.es: Programas de FQHC con escala deslizante y subvenciones de fertilidad: los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) en Oregón típicamente no realizan FIV, pero las subvenciones de fertilidad a través de RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association y Baby Quest Foundation pueden reducir los costos de bolsillo en $1,500 a $15,000 para pacientes calificados.

items.en: Add-on costs: PGT genetic testing adds $3,000 to $6,000; ICSI adds $1,000 to $2,000; donor eggs add $20,000 to $35,000 beyond the base cycle cost; gestational carrier arrangements add $60,000 to $150,000 in total legal and medical costs. Each add-on is optional but may be medically recommended depending on patient age, diagnosis, and embryo quality.
items.es: Costos de complementos: las pruebas genéticas PGT agregan $3,000 a $6,000; el ICSI agrega $1,000 a $2,000; los óvulos de donante agregan $20,000 a $35,000 más allá del costo del ciclo base; los acuerdos de portadora gestacional agregan $60,000 a $150,000 en costos legales y médicos totales.

intro.en: Oregon IVF billing is complex and itemized. Because Oregon has no state insurance mandate as of mid-2026, most patients are paying self-pay rates with no insurer backstop to catch errors. If your final Oregon IVF bill significantly exceeds your clinic's upfront Good Faith Estimate, check for these common billing errors before paying:
intro.es: La facturación de FIV en Oregón es compleja y detallada. Debido a que Oregón no tiene mandato estatal de seguro a mediados de 2026, la mayoría de los pacientes pagan tarifas de pago propio sin un respaldo de aseguradora para detectar errores. Si su factura final de FIV en Oregón supera significativamente el Estimado de Buena Fe inicial de la clínica, verifique estos errores comunes antes de pagar:

items.en: ICSI billed on all eggs retrieved when the procedure was only performed on a subset. Request the embryology lab report and verify the number of eggs where ICSI was actually applied versus the number billed.
items.es: ICSI facturado en todos los óvulos recuperados cuando el procedimiento solo se realizó en un subconjunto. Solicite el informe del laboratorio de embriología y verifique el número de óvulos donde se aplicó realmente el ICSI versus el número facturado.

items.en: PGT biopsy fees charged for embryos that did not develop to a biopsiable stage (Day 5 or Day 6 blastocyst) due to developmental arrest. Request the embryology cycle summary before paying the PGT invoice, and verify each line item against the number of blastocysts that actually underwent biopsy.
items.es: Tarifas de biopsia PGT cobradas por embriones que no se desarrollaron hasta una etapa de biopsia (blastocisto del Día 5 o Día 6) debido al arresto del desarrollo. Solicite el resumen del ciclo de embriología antes de pagar la factura de PGT y verifique cada elemento contra el número de blastocistos que realmente se sometieron a biopsia.

items.en: Anesthesia billed by a separate out-of-network provider not included in the base cycle package. Under the No Surprises Act, unexpected out-of-network anesthesia charges may constitute a surprise bill. Confirm the anesthesia provider's network status before the egg retrieval procedure.
items.es: Anestesia facturada por un proveedor separado fuera de la red no incluido en el paquete del ciclo base. Bajo la Ley de No Sorpresas, los cargos inesperados de anestesia fuera de la red pueden constituir una factura sorpresa. Confirme el estado de la red del proveedor de anestesia antes del procedimiento de recuperación de óvulos.

items.en: Medications billed at retail pharmacy prices when a specialty pharmacy discount or clinic-dispensed price was available at a lower cost. Ask whether the clinic partners with a specialty pharmacy and what the contracted price difference is versus a standard retail pharmacy.
items.es: Medicamentos facturados a precios de farmacia minorista cuando estaba disponible un descuento de farmacia especializada o un precio dispensado por la clínica a menor costo. Pregunte si la clínica se asocia con una farmacia especializada y cuál es la diferencia de precio contratada versus una farmacia minorista estándar.

items.en: Frozen embryo transfer billed at the full fresh cycle rate when a lower FET rate was quoted in the original Good Faith Estimate. Compare the FET line item on the final bill to the FET line item on your written estimate before paying.
items.es: Transferencia de embrión congelado facturada a la tarifa de ciclo fresco completo cuando se cotizó una tarifa de TEC más baja en el Estimado de Buena Fe original. Compare el elemento de TEC en la factura final con el elemento de TEC en su estimado escrito antes de pagar.

items.en: Monitoring visit charges billed at the hospital outpatient rate when the clinic is a standalone independent center. Independent Oregon fertility clinics should bill at independent-clinic rates, not hospital outpatient facility rates. Check the facility code on your Explanation of Benefits or itemized bill.
items.es: Cargos de visitas de monitoreo facturados a la tarifa de hospital ambulatorio cuando la clínica es un centro independiente autónomo. Las clínicas de fertilidad independientes de Oregón deben facturar a las tarifas de clínica independiente, no a las tarifas de instalación hospitalaria ambulatoria. Verifique el código de instalación en su Explicación de Beneficios o factura detallada.

en.question: How much does IVF cost in Oregon without insurance in 2026?
en.answer: Without insurance, a standard IVF cycle in Oregon costs $12,000 to $15,000 for the base procedure at independent Portland-area fertility clinics in 2026, and $15,000 to $22,000 at hospital-affiliated or national-network centers. Adding fertility medications ($3,000 to $7,000) brings the all-in total to approximately $15,000 to $22,000 at independent clinics and up to $30,000 at more expensive centers. Optional add-ons such as PGT genetic testing ($3,000 to $6,000) and ICSI ($1,000 to $2,000) increase costs further. Patients who need 2 to 3 cycles may spend $30,000 to $90,000 over the full course of treatment. The Fertility Center of Oregon publishes a global fee of approximately $12,500 that includes monitoring, retrieval, ICSI, and one transfer with cryopreservation.

en.question: Does Medicare cover IVF in Oregon?
en.answer: No. Medicare does not cover IVF under Original Medicare Part A, Medicare Part B, or Part D, regardless of state. This federal program-level exclusion applies equally in Oregon. The 2026 Medicare Part B deductible of $283 and the standard 20% coinsurance apply only to covered services; because IVF is excluded from Medicare entirely, no Medicare deductible or coinsurance calculation applies to IVF costs. A small number of Medicare Advantage plans offer supplemental fertility-related benefits voluntarily, but IVF coverage is not required and is uncommon. Medigap supplemental plans also do not cover IVF because Medigap supplements only the services Original Medicare covers.

en.question: How do I request a Good Faith Estimate for IVF from an Oregon fertility clinic?
en.answer: Under the No Surprises Act (effective January 1, 2022), every Oregon fertility clinic must provide a written Good Faith Estimate to self-pay and uninsured patients before treatment begins. Call the clinic's financial coordinator and identify yourself as self-pay or uninsured. Request an itemized written estimate listing the base cycle HCPCS code (S4015 for fresh cycle, S4016 for frozen embryo transfer), anesthesia, laboratory fees, monitoring visit fees, and any agreed add-ons such as ICSI, PGT, and embryo storage. For an egg retrieval scheduled 10 or more business days out, you are entitled to the estimate at least 3 business days before service. Keep the written estimate. If your final Oregon IVF bill exceeds it by $400 or more, you have 120 days from the bill date to file a dispute at cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

en.question: What is the No Surprises Act and does it apply to IVF in Oregon?
en.answer: The No Surprises Act, effective January 1, 2022, is a federal law that protects self-pay and uninsured patients from unexpected medical bills. The No Surprises Act applies to all healthcare providers and facilities in Oregon, including all fertility clinics, hospital-affiliated reproductive medicine centers, and independent IVF laboratories. Under the law, any Oregon patient who is uninsured or paying cash for IVF has the right to a written Good Faith Estimate of expected charges before treatment begins. If the actual bill exceeds the Good Faith Estimate by $400 or more, the patient can submit a patient-provider dispute resolution (PPDR) claim within 120 days through the federal portal at cms.gov/nosurprisesact. The law does not cap IVF prices, but it creates an enforceable pre-treatment pricing commitment for self-pay patients at every Oregon fertility clinic.

en.question: How do I get a written cash-pay quote for IVF in Oregon?
en.answer: Call the financial coordinator at two or three Oregon fertility clinics and ask for their self-pay or fee-for-service IVF price list. Request: the base cycle fee (and what it includes), the frozen embryo transfer fee, and any fees billed separately such as anesthesia, laboratory fees, and monitoring. Ask whether the clinic offers a cash-pay discount for prompt payment, typically 10 to 25 percent off the listed price. Ask about multi-cycle packages or shared-risk programs, which can reduce the per-cycle cost by 15 to 25 percent. Get all quotes in writing as a Good Faith Estimate under the No Surprises Act before you schedule any procedure. Compare at least two Oregon clinics before committing. The Fertility Center of Oregon, Spring Fertility Portland, Pinnacle Fertility (formerly ORM Fertility), and Oregon Fertility Institute are among the larger Portland-area clinics to compare.

en.question: Can I negotiate an IVF bill after the fact in Oregon?
en.answer: Yes. If your final Oregon IVF bill exceeds your original Good Faith Estimate by $400 or more, you can file a federal patient-provider dispute resolution (PPDR) claim within 120 days of the bill date at cms.gov/nosurprisesact. Outside of the formal PPDR process, many Oregon fertility clinics will negotiate a cash-pay settlement, especially if you offer prompt payment. Typical reductions for cash-pay-now offers run 20 to 40 percent off the remaining balance. Ask the billing office to itemize every charge and identify any line items you believe were added in error. Common billing errors in Oregon IVF include ICSI charged on all eggs when applied to only a subset, and PGT fees on embryos that did not develop to a biopsiable stage.

en.question: What is the difference between hospital-affiliated and independent IVF clinic costs in Oregon?
en.answer: Independent Oregon fertility clinics in the Portland area, such as the Fertility Center of Oregon, typically charge $12,000 to $15,000 for a fresh base IVF cycle in 2026. Hospital-affiliated or national-network centers, such as Spring Fertility Portland (which partners with OHSU) and Oregon Fertility Institute, charge $15,000 to $22,000 or more for a base cycle, not including medications. The clinical procedure is identical between settings: egg retrieval, fertilization, embryo culture, and transfer. The price differential reflects facility overhead, lab infrastructure, and ancillary billing practices. SART (Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology) success rate data should be reviewed alongside cost data to make a full comparison. For most self-pay Oregon patients, an independent clinic is the highest-impact cost-reduction option.

en.question: Does Oregon law or the ACA require insurance to cover IVF?
en.answer: Neither the ACA nor Oregon state law currently requires health insurance to cover IVF. The ACA lists essential health benefits but fertility treatment is not among them at the federal level. Oregon's HB4155 (2026), which would have required commercial insurers and the state public employee benefit boards to cover IVF, died in the Joint Ways and Means Committee before the 2026 session adjourned, according to RESOLVE's Oregon bill tracking. Oregon has no enacted IVF insurance mandate as of mid-2026. Some Oregon employers voluntarily include fertility benefits or contract with fertility-benefit platforms like Progyny or Carrot. Oregon's ACA marketplace plans do not have a standard IVF benefit, but individual plan documents may include it as a voluntary benefit. The Oregon Health Plan (OHP, Oregon's Medicaid program) excludes IVF from its Prioritized List of covered services.

en.question: What is the difference between IVF and IUI, and which is more likely to be covered by insurance in Oregon?
en.answer: IUI (intrauterine insemination) is a less invasive and far less expensive fertility procedure that places prepared sperm directly into the uterus during ovulation. IUI typically costs $300 to $1,500 per cycle in Oregon and does not require egg retrieval or an external fertilization lab. IVF costs 10 to 20 times more per cycle but generally has higher per-cycle success rates, especially for patients over 35 or with diagnosed infertility conditions. Because Oregon has no IVF or IUI insurance mandate as of mid-2026, neither procedure has mandatory commercial insurance coverage in the state. Employers who voluntarily include fertility benefits often cover both IUI and IVF. Some Oregon employer plans and fertility-benefit platforms cover IUI at a lower cost-sharing tier than IVF, making IUI the first step for many patients before moving to IVF.

en.question: Are there HCPCS billing codes for IVF in Oregon?
en.answer: Yes. The primary public-domain HCPCS Level II codes used for IVF billing are: S4015 (complete IVF cycle, case rate) for fresh cycles; S4016 (frozen IVF cycle, case rate) for frozen embryo transfers; and S4017 (incomplete cycle, cancelled before stimulation, case rate). These codes are public domain and used by commercial insurers in Oregon and nationally. Medicare excludes IVF and does not process claims under these codes. Always ask your Oregon fertility clinic to provide their itemized billing codes in the Good Faith Estimate so you can verify that charges on the final bill match services actually rendered.

es.question: ¿Cuánto cuesta la FIV en Oregón sin seguro en 2026?
es.answer: Sin seguro, un ciclo estándar de FIV en Oregón cuesta de $12,000 a $15,000 por el procedimiento base en clínicas de fertilidad independientes del área de Portland en 2026, y de $15,000 a $22,000 en centros afiliados a hospitales o de redes nacionales. Agregar medicamentos de fertilidad ($3,000 a $7,000) lleva el total a aproximadamente $15,000 a $22,000 en clínicas independientes y hasta $30,000 en centros más costosos. Los complementos opcionales como las pruebas genéticas PGT ($3,000 a $6,000) y el ICSI ($1,000 a $2,000) aumentan aún más los costos. Los pacientes que necesitan 2 a 3 ciclos pueden gastar de $30,000 a $90,000 durante el tratamiento completo.

es.question: ¿Cubre Medicare la FIV en Oregón?
es.answer: No. Medicare no cubre la FIV bajo el Medicare Original Parte A, Medicare Parte B ni la Parte D, independientemente del estado. Esta exclusión a nivel de programa federal aplica igualmente en Oregón. El deducible de Medicare Parte B 2026 de $283 y el coseguro estándar del 20% solo aplican a los servicios cubiertos; como la FIV está excluida de Medicare completamente, no aplica ningún cálculo de deducible o coseguro de Medicare para los costos de FIV. Un pequeño número de planes Medicare Advantage ofrecen beneficios suplementarios relacionados con la fertilidad voluntariamente, pero la cobertura de FIV no es obligatoria y es poco común. Los planes suplementarios Medigap tampoco cubren la FIV.

es.question: ¿Cómo solicito un Estimado de Buena Fe para FIV en una clínica de fertilidad de Oregón?
es.answer: Bajo la Ley de No Sorpresas (vigente desde el 1 de enero de 2022), cada clínica de fertilidad de Oregón debe proporcionar un Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito a los pacientes que pagan de su bolsillo o no tienen seguro antes de que comience el tratamiento. Llame al coordinador financiero de la clínica e identifíquese como paciente de pago propio o sin seguro. Solicite un estimado escrito detallado que liste el código del ciclo base (HCPCS S4015 para ciclo fresco, S4016 para ciclo congelado), anestesia, honorarios de laboratorio y todos los complementos acordados como ICSI, PGT y almacenamiento de embriones. Conserve el estimado escrito. Si su factura final supera el estimado en $400 o más, tiene 120 días para presentar una disputa en cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

es.question: ¿Qué es la Ley de No Sorpresas y aplica a la FIV en Oregón?
es.answer: La Ley de No Sorpresas, vigente desde el 1 de enero de 2022, es una ley federal que protege a los pacientes que pagan de su bolsillo o no tienen seguro de facturas médicas inesperadas. Aplica a todos los proveedores de atención médica e instalaciones en Oregón, incluidas las clínicas de fertilidad, los centros de medicina reproductiva afiliados a hospitales y los laboratorios de FIV independientes. Bajo la ley, cualquier paciente de Oregón que no tenga seguro o pague en efectivo por la FIV tiene derecho a un Estimado de Buena Fe por escrito de los cargos esperados antes de que comience el tratamiento. Si la factura real supera el Estimado de Buena Fe en $400 o más, el paciente puede presentar una reclamación PPDR dentro de 120 días a través del portal federal en cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

es.question: ¿Cómo obtengo una cotización de pago en efectivo por escrito para FIV en Oregón?
es.answer: Llame al coordinador financiero de dos o tres clínicas de fertilidad de Oregón y solicite su lista de precios de FIV de pago propio o pago por servicio. Solicite específicamente: la tarifa del ciclo base (y qué incluye), la tarifa de transferencia de embrión congelado y cualquier tarifa que se facture por separado como anestesia, honorarios de laboratorio y monitoreo. Pregunte si la clínica ofrece un descuento de pago en efectivo por pago puntual, típicamente del 10 al 25 por ciento del precio listado. Pregunte sobre paquetes de múltiples ciclos o programas de riesgo compartido, que pueden reducir el costo por ciclo en un 15 a 25 por ciento. Obtenga todas las cotizaciones por escrito como Estimado de Buena Fe bajo la Ley de No Sorpresas antes de programar cualquier procedimiento.

es.question: ¿Puedo negociar una factura de FIV después del hecho en Oregón?
es.answer: Sí. Si su factura final de FIV en Oregón supera su Estimado de Buena Fe original en $400 o más, puede presentar una reclamación federal de resolución de disputas entre paciente y proveedor (PPDR) dentro de los 120 días de la fecha de la factura en cms.gov/nosurprisesact. Fuera del proceso PPDR formal, muchas clínicas de fertilidad de Oregón negociarán un acuerdo de pago en efectivo, especialmente si usted ofrece pagar con prontitud. Las reducciones típicas para las ofertas de pago en efectivo inmediato son del 20 al 40 por ciento del saldo restante. Solicite a la oficina de facturación que detalle cada cargo e identifique cualquier elemento que crea que se agregó por error.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre los costos de clínicas de FIV afiliadas a hospitales e independientes en Oregón?
es.answer: Las clínicas de fertilidad independientes de Oregón en el área de Portland, como el Fertility Center of Oregon, típicamente cobran de $12,000 a $15,000 por un ciclo base fresco de FIV en 2026. Los centros afiliados a hospitales o de redes nacionales, como Spring Fertility Portland (que se asocia con OHSU) y Oregon Fertility Institute, cobran de $15,000 a $22,000 o más por un ciclo base, sin incluir medicamentos. El procedimiento clínico es idéntico entre los dos entornos. Para la mayoría de los pacientes de pago propio en Oregón, una clínica independiente es la opción de reducción de costos de mayor impacto disponible.

es.question: ¿Exige la ley de Oregón o el ACA que el seguro cubra la FIV?
es.answer: Ni el ACA ni la ley estatal de Oregón requieren actualmente que el seguro de salud cubra la FIV. El ACA enumera los beneficios esenciales de salud pero el tratamiento de fertilidad no está entre ellos a nivel federal. El HB4155 de Oregón (2026), que habría requerido que las aseguradoras comerciales y los consejos de beneficios de empleados del estado cubrieran la FIV, murió en el Comité Conjunto de Vías y Medios antes de que se levantara la sesión 2026. El Oregon Health Plan (OHP), el programa Medicaid de Oregón, excluye la FIV de su Lista Priorizada de servicios cubiertos. Algunos empleadores de Oregón incluyen voluntariamente beneficios de fertilidad o contratan con plataformas como Progyny o Carrot.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre la FIV y la IIU, y cuál es más probable que esté cubierta por el seguro en Oregón?
es.answer: La IIU (inseminación intrauterina) es un procedimiento de fertilidad menos invasivo y mucho menos costoso que coloca esperma preparado directamente en el útero durante la ovulación. La IIU típicamente cuesta de $300 a $1,500 por ciclo en Oregón y no requiere recuperación de óvulos ni un laboratorio de fertilización externo. La FIV cuesta de 10 a 20 veces más por ciclo pero generalmente tiene tasas de éxito por ciclo más altas. Debido a que Oregón no tiene mandato de seguro para FIV ni para IIU a mediados de 2026, ninguno de los procedimientos tiene cobertura de seguro comercial obligatoria en el estado. Los empleadores que voluntariamente incluyen beneficios de fertilidad a menudo cubren tanto la IIU como la FIV.

es.question: ¿Hay códigos de facturación HCPCS para la FIV en Oregón?
es.answer: Sí. Los principales códigos HCPCS Nivel II de dominio público utilizados para la facturación de FIV son: S4015 (ciclo completo de FIV, tarifa por caso) para ciclos frescos; S4016 (ciclo de FIV congelado, tarifa por caso) para transferencias de embriones congelados; y S4017 (ciclo incompleto, cancelado antes de la estimulación, tarifa por caso). Estos códigos son de dominio público y son utilizados por aseguradoras comerciales en Oregón y a nivel nacional. Medicare excluye la FIV y no procesa reclamaciones bajo estos códigos. Siempre solicite a su clínica de fertilidad de Oregón que proporcione sus códigos de facturación detallados en el Estimado de Buena Fe para verificar que los cargos en la factura final coincidan con los servicios realmente prestados.

en: how much does IVF cost in Oregon
es: estimacion de buena fe FIV Oregon

numberedSteps: Contact the Oregon fertility clinic's financial coordinator and identify yourself as self-pay or uninsured, or request an itemized pre-treatment cost estimate even if you have some insurance.

Request a written Good Faith Estimate listing the base cycle HCPCS code (S4015 for fresh cycle, S4016 for frozen embryo transfer), anesthesia, laboratory fees, monitoring visit fees, and all optional add-ons such as ICSI, PGT, and embryo cryopreservation.
Provide your ZIP code and share the specific IVF protocol your Oregon reproductive endocrinologist has recommended, including the expected stimulation dose range.

Confirm the timing rule: if your egg retrieval is scheduled 10 or more business days out, you are entitled to the written estimate at least 3 business days before service. If scheduled 3 to 9 business days out, 1 business day before service.

Keep the written Good Faith Estimate. If your final Oregon IVF bill exceeds the estimate by $400 or more, you have 120 days from the bill date to file a patient-provider dispute resolution (PPDR) claim at cms.gov/nosurprisesact.

Prior infertility diagnostic test results (AMH level, FSH level, antral follicle count ultrasound)
Physician referral or reproductive endocrinologist treatment plan
List of current medications and supplements
Prior cycle records if this is not your first IVF cycle
Employer benefits summary or Summary Plan Description if you believe you may have voluntary fertility coverage
commonReasonsQuoteChanges: Additional monitoring appointments required by your specific stimulation response (more ultrasounds and blood draws than the standard protocol estimate assumed)
Medication adjustments mid-cycle based on follicle development, increasing or decreasing the dosage and therefore the medication cost
Unexpected embryo development outcomes requiring a different number of PGT biopsies than originally planned
Anesthesia billed by a separate provider not included in the base cycle package, potentially out-of-network
Embryo storage fees for additional embryos beyond what the original estimate assumed
Cycle cancellation fees if the retrieval or transfer is cancelled after stimulation has begun (HCPCS S4017)

selfPayPrograms.typicalDiscountRange: 10 to 25 percent below published chargemaster cash price for self-pay prompt-payment negotiations; 15 to 25 percent per-cycle savings through multi-cycle packages
howToAsk: Call before scheduling and ask: 'What is your self-pay or fee-for-service IVF price for a fresh cycle, and is there a cash-payment discount?'
Get the complete itemized price in writing as a Good Faith Estimate under the No Surprises Act before signing any financial agreement or beginning treatment
Ask specifically whether anesthesia, lab fees, and monitoring visits are included in the base cycle price or billed separately on top of the quoted rate
Ask about multi-cycle or shared-risk package pricing: these are typically 15 to 25 percent less expensive per cycle than paying cycle by cycle
Ask about same-day or same-week payment discounts: some Oregon clinics offer 5 to 15 percent off for prompt cash payment
Compare the self-pay cash price to any insurance negotiated rate before deciding which to use
